accuracy.evidence: Every correspondence was checked against the English National Curriculum Year 2 spelling appendix: /dʒ/ as -ge and -dge (dge straight after a short vowel: badge, bridge, fudge; ge after a long vowel or consonant: cage, huge, large), /s/ as c before e, i, y (city, ice, fancy), /n/ as kn and gn, /r/ as wr, /ʒ/ as s (treasure, television). The no-final-j rule is stated as almost never, with Raj as a borrowed exception, so nothing is overstated.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented Year 1-2 decoding errors: reading every c as k (city prediction, cee step, cell challenge), sounding the silent letter (knot prediction, wrong and gnome challenge items, m5 k-nock), treating dge as separate sounds (m10 counts badge as 3 sounds), using dge after a long vowel (cage and huge in the ends step, huge challenge item) and ending a word in j (endj feedback).

lab_distinct.evidence: flagaltsp is built on one sound with several graphemes: sound houses that each hold several spellings, a letter hunt where silent letters must be tapped as part of the grapheme, dge/ge magnets chosen by the vowel length before the gap, and a soft-c reader that highlights the letter after c. It does not repeat the digraph lab's two-letters-one-sound magnets; highest 6-token overlap with any other flagship is 4.7% (flag_dgraph).

lab_teaches.evidence: The child finds each rule by acting: posting cage and giraffe into the j house shows one sound with two spellings, tapping only n in knot is answered with a prompt to find the quiet partner letter, the ends step names the vowel sound before every choice, and the cee step highlights the next letter so the e, i, y pattern is seen before the done message states it.

predictions.evidence: Four locked predictions, each with a tempting wrong option that the next task disproves: each sound has just one spelling (the houses hold two or three), yes k-not (the hunt needs k and n together), ge after a short vowel (badge and fudge take dge), and c always says k (city, ice and fancy say s). The done message reports the prediction back.

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six rotating questions with shuffled options and a separate message for every wrong option, e.g. the g in gnome makes no sound; c is before e here so it says s; the u in huge is long so just ge; saying it loud does not change wr; giant spells j with g while dge follows a short vowel. Wrong taps in the lab also name the slip, such as the vowel length before the gap.

readability.evidence: Kid explanation scores Flesch-Kincaid grade -0.3 and the adult text 8.2, inside the family limits of 5.0 and 10.0. Canvas words are single words and short sentences, the key term grapheme is defined in the first step, and every target word is decodable by a Year 2 reader.

no_filler.evidence: Each paragraph carries a correspondence, a rule or a mistake to watch for; no praise padding. The explanation stays under the 12% overlap limit with Vowel Digraphs, Consonant Digraphs and Single Letter Sounds, and the lab's done messages each state the rule just found rather than repeating a template.

mobile.evidence: Screenshots at 360 px Android in dark and light for every step: three sound houses fit side by side with their spelling lists and ticks, eight letter tiles for treasure fit on one row, and the picture now sits above the hu_ gap so the prefix no longer touches it. Every canvas target is at least 56 px tall and has a large button twin below.

accessibility.evidence: walk.cjs: all four tasks finish with Show me on desktop and iPhone 13 and axe-core finds no WCAG 2.1 AA violations in light or dark theme. Every drag (word to house, dge or ge to the gap) and tap (letters, k or s pads) has a labelled button twin, e.g. Post city in the s sound house, and each result is spoken through the polite live region and the canvas aria-label.
